change.description: Move managed task timeline intervals from SSE rows to fixed-watermark HTTP pages and afterRevision deltas, with marker-only SSE v2 notifications.
change.release_unit_description: Managed task timeline API and SSE v2 contract, including fixed-watermark HTTP paging and revision catch-up.

planned.reasoning: The timeline SSE schema epoch changes from v1 interval rows to v2 revision markers, so consumers of the old payload must migrate to HTTP pages. The persisted timeline schema and existing task controls, colors, request timestamps, and duration semantics are unchanged.

scope_drift.description: This candidate changes the public timeline SSE payload from interval snapshots/deltas to a v2 revision marker; consumers of the v1 payload must migrate to the HTTP timeline endpoint.

current.reasoning: The timeline SSE schema epoch changes to /v2 and removes segment rows from notifications, which is a breaking public API change. The maintenance-store schema, control columns, and legacy history semantics are unchanged by this transport change.

verified.reasoning: Transport tests verify the v2 marker-only SSE contract and unchanged paginated HTTP response; the public SSE payload change is intentionally breaking while persistent-state compatibility remains at the prior minor level.

public_api.supported_consumer_range: Consumers that expect interval rows in system.managed-tasks.timeline/v1 must migrate to schema epoch /v2 and load interval rows through the paginated HTTP timeline endpoint; workload response fields and enabled-only task updates remain compatible additions.

persistent_state.state_description: Existing maintenance controls and task-run history plus stable colors, actual execution boundaries, task-deferral intervals, observation sessions, coverage revisions, and bounded per-task workload samples.
persistent_state.source_program_compatibility_range: The candidate reads supported earlier-minor maintenance databases with the task tables; older minors need not read the new workload table, and direct major skips remain unsupported. Persistent-state impact is minor.
